text:
Ilya Sorokin turned away all 37 shots he faced, and by the numbers he stopped about 4.05 goals' worth of chances, which is the whole story of a 6-0 game that the replays say New Jersey had a better claim to winning. NJD piled up 72 shot attempts to 50 and out-created the Islanders 4.05 expected goals to 3.63. Run the game a thousand times and the Devils come out ahead 56 percent of the time. This was not one of those nights.

The Islanders did their damage in a few quick bursts. Simon Holmstrom opened the scoring 3:32 into the second period, and Brayden Schenn made it 2-0 less than two minutes later on a snap shot the model gave a 30 percent chance. Bo Horvat added a power-play goal at 12:08, and the lead was three before New Jersey had a single goal to show for a period in which it generated 2.24 expected goals to 1.49. Nico Daws, meanwhile, allowed six on 32 shots against roughly 3.63 expected, a gap of about 2.37 goals.

The third period pushed it out of reach. Victor Eklund scored at 11:32 and Ondrej Palat followed at 12:14, two goals in 42 seconds, and Casey Cizikas capped it with a short-handed goal at 18:41. Matthew Schaefer had two assists and led all skaters with 20:36 of ice time, and Eklund and Schenn each finished with a goal and an assist. New York also took 9 takeaways to 3 and won the hits battle 25 to 15, but the margin came from the crease. Sorokin was the difference, and he was the second star behind Eklund.
